A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RECALL. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-success, runtime, semantic-alignment and ablation results across ten unlearning methods and four tasks.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark, comparator, diversity and robustness evaluations.

M1.justification: v1 Equation 15 and Algorithm 1 use additive reference-latent integration. v2 Equation 9 changes this to a convex blend, but Algorithm 1, line 20, retains the additive update. This inconsistency prevents establishing which procedure defines v2; the remaining framework and loss are retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMA adversarially optimized prompts and ART benign red-teaming prompts to the nudity evaluation, beyond the retained I2P coverage. Appendix G.5 also introduces partially aligned and unrelated reference-image conditions. The original four target concepts remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CCE and WACE-N/WACE-C against the original tasks. CCE and WACE also enter semantic and qualitative comparisons. The diversity comparison expands beyond Text-only/Image-only to additional controls and competing attacks, while the runtime comparison replaces P4D-K with WACE-C.

E3.justification: Diversity evaluation adds DINO and replaces the UCE-only LPIPS/IS comparison with an ESD/UCE comparison using broader controls. New protocols vary DDIM/LMS/PNDM schedulers, 10–50 sampling steps, integration intervals and coefficients. The principal 50-DDIM-step, 20-update attack configuration remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds scheduler and step-budget sensitivity, first-success-step distributions, integration-parameter sweeps and reference-alignment failure tests. It expands comparative diversity analysis. The earlier binary integration ablation is replaced by sweeps, while v1's explicit noise-initialization comparison in Table 7 is not retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies global random seed 2025 and explains its relationship to task-specific generation seeds. Both versions provide example/reference seeds. No increased repeated-run count, confidence intervals or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds CCE/WACE results, RECALL average ASRs of 88.20% on MMA and 65.44% on ART, and DINO and sensitivity results. Original Table 1 entries and SD 2.x results are retained. The earlier cross-method LPIPS/IS table and explicit noise-initialization results disappear; the additions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.4 defines the recovery target through the original model's output for the same prompt. v2 Section 3.3 formally allows target-concept images from any source, aligning the formulation with reference sources already permitted by v1. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The attack novelty and effectiveness, efficiency and semantic-fidelity claims remain. v2 explicitly adds model-owner robustness auditing to the abstract, introduction and conclusion, refining the claimed contribution and intended use of the existing white-box framework.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of reference-mismatch failures, scheduler insensitivity and integration tradeoffs. The conclusion replaces v1's background-bias/diversity limitation with different future-work priorities. Appendix F.2 also makes stronger comparative diversity interpretations, although Figure 8 does not consistently support the claimed superiority over weak controls.

D1.justification: v2 discloses top-10 style and top-1 object-classification rules, explicitly describes final image-generation sampling in Algorithm 1, and explains that zero runtime denotes fewer than five successful prompts. It adds implementation links for new baselines. Core hyperparameters, hardware and the RECALL repository remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds CCE and WACE, distinguishing embedding-based and noise-based attacks. Citations also expand to MMA, DINOv2 and additional adversarial research, while several background references disappear. The central novelty positioning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites or condenses the abstract, related work, threat model and conclusion; removes the standalone Stable Diffusion background; separates generalizability from ablations; and reorganizes the appendices. Ethics, reproducibility and acknowledgment sections are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column ACM to single-column ICLR formatting. Figure 2 is redrawn, Tables 1–2 expand, full qualitative and efficiency comparisons move into appendices, and new diversity and robustness plots substantially extend the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: MMA/ART evaluations, CCE/WACE comparisons and reference-mismatch tests strengthen evidence about generalization and failure conditions. The net gain is limited by the new Equation 9/Algorithm 1 inconsistency, diversity interpretations contradicted by parts of Figure 8, and removal of the explicit noise-initialization comparison. The broader evaluation improves the paper, but these reporting regressions weaken its clarity and reproducibility.
